subject: URGENT: NimbusPay VPC latency surge - exec escalation
messages:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@nimbuspay.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: susan.li@nimbuspay.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — urgent

Hi Sean / Monica,

We started seeing a spike in 95th/99th latency and increased 5xx errors on our private VPC deployment at ~08:45 PST. The latency jump is across all routes but is most visible on the auth/token and chat endpoints. Throughput is normal but tail latency and error rate are unacceptable for our SLAs.

Attached is a snapshot of logs and a small flamegraph we pulled (nimbuspay_error_snapshot_20260321.tar.gz). We rolled a config change yesterday (reduced KV cache TTL + enable_strict_batching=true) but the timeline suggests the spike correlates with that.

Can Redwood escalate to engineering? Our execs are pressing for a remediation plan — we may need a hotfix/rollback if this persists.

Alex
Alex Tan
CTO, NimbusPay

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@nimbuspay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — urgent

Thanks Alex — we see the alerts on our side as well. Monica and I are triaging now. Rishi / Dev: can you please pick this up as priority P0?

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: can you pull the inference node CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, and KV cache hit rates for the last hour?
- Dev: can you validate the recent config change (enable_strict_batching) in the NimbusPay config set and whether it was propagated cluster-wide?
- Monica: I'll set up a short sync with the customer and loop in sales leadership if exec engagement is needed.

Alex — we aim to have a short incident update within 30 minutes and a recommended mitigation (rollback or config tweak) within 90 minutes.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — urgent

Quick debugging notes (pulling live metrics now):
- Node metrics: GPU utilization steady at 48-52% across pods; CPU on the control plane nodes spiked to 85% for ~6m starting 08:46 PST.
- Queue lengths: request queue latency increased; batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 tokens for many requests (so batching efficiency dropped sharply).
- KV cache hit rate: dropped from 78% baseline to ~12% around 08:45.
- Error profile: majority are transient KV cache misses causing fallback to cold-start attention paths, plus a handful of OOMs on one worker (OOMs correlate with a mid-day surge in sequence length).

Preliminary hypothesis: The recent TTL reduction for per-customer KV entries + strict batching toggled an eviction pattern that lost hot prefixes, which combined with certain long-sequence requests caused cache pressure and degraded batch formation. This produced more cold calls and degraded throughput/latency.

Next steps proposed:
1) Temporarily revert KV TTL to previous value and disable enable_strict_batching for NimbusPay config (canary first).
2) Increase cache capacity on the worker group handling high-seq traffic by +25% and monitor hit rate.
3) If OOMs persist, scale an extra worker for the affected pool.

I can push the canary rollback within 20 minutes if we have approval. I will also attach the sampling logs to the internal ticket.

— Rishi
Lead Inference Engineer
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@nimbuspay.com>, Susan Li <susan.li@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — exec escalation

Alex / Susan — update and proposed immediate mitigation:
- Root cause hypothesis: unintended KV cache evictions after yesterday's KV TTL change combined with strict batching settings.
- Immediate mitigation (canary today): revert KV TTL to previous value and disable enable_strict_batching on 2 of 6 worker pools; increase cache capacity on the hot pool +1 replica.
- If canary stabilizes metrics within 20 minutes we will roll to remaining pools. Rishi will monitor hit rates and queue lengths continuously.

Request: Alex, do you approve the canary rollback? We plan to run the canary at 10:20 PST and will pause/rollback if any negative regression.

Also looping in Laura (sales leadership) for visibility and to coordinate an exec readout if required.

— Sean
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@nimbuspay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — exec escalation

Alex — thanks for the quick signal. Approve the canary rollback. Laura — quick ask: our execs may be pulled in if the canary does not stabilize within the next hour. Can you be on standby to join a 15min call if NimbusPay requests CTO-to-CTO?

I attached a short runbook snapshot we will follow (runbook_vpc_tuning_v1.pdf) and I'll take notes in a shared doc (meeting_notes_20260322.txt).

— Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@nimbuspay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in our VPC deployment — exec escalation

Final incident summary and next steps (post-canary):
- Timeline: 08:45 PST 3/21 — latency/5xx spike begins. 10:20 PST 3/21 — canary revert executed (KV TTL + disable_strict_batching) on 2 pools. 10:40 PST — metrics returned to baseline on canary pools. 11:15 PST — full rollout completed.
- Impact: 95th latency returned to baseline within canary window; 99th latency improved but a residual tail persisted (investigating long-seq handling). Error rate returned to <0.1% post-rollout.
- Root cause: KV TTL reduction caused rapid eviction of hot prefixes; strict batching prevented effective coalescing under this eviction pattern, producing more cold starts and OOM pressure at the worker level.
- Permanent remediation actions:
  * Update default KV TTL recommendation for VPC/private deployments in the onboarding docs.
  * Add an automated alert for sudden KV cache hit-rate drops (INC-1129).
  * Implement a conservative fallback policy for strict batching that favors batch formation under cache-pressure scenarios.
  * Add a small buffer to cache allocations on high-variance tenants for 30 days post-config change.
- Customer next steps: we agreed to a joint post-incident review on Monday 3/23 at 09:00 PST (calendar invite sent).
- Compensation: Laura will coordinate potential goodwill credits if requested by NimbusPay; we'll keep the ask to the executive team pending the post-incident review.

I'll attach the incident artifacts to INC-1129 and share the Drive link. Thanks to the on-call and CS teams for the fast response.

— Sean
